body:
## Summary
Implement a wiki-first docs workflow and make GitHub Pages product-first by publishing the offline studio demo at root with a docs-to-wiki redirect.

## Linked Issues
- https://github.com/ringxworld/story_generator/issues/25

## Motivation / Context
The current public surfaces are split in a way that makes docs discovery inconsistent and puts documentation ahead of product UX on Pages. This change sets a clear contract: docs are mirrored to wiki, and Pages shows the product snapshot first.

## What Changed
- Added `tools/sync_wiki.py` to mirror `docs/` markdown and ADR files into the GitHub wiki structure, including generated `_Sidebar.md` and `_Footer.md`.
- Added `make wiki-sync` and `make wiki-sync-push` targets.
- Added ADR `0018` for the wiki/docs + product-first Pages decision.
- Updated deployment and collaboration docs with wiki sync workflow and surface ownership.
- Updated Pages deploy workflow to publish offline studio demo at root and keep `/studio` as compatibility alias.
- Added `/docs` redirect page in Pages artifacts that sends users to the repo wiki.
- Updated repository contract tests for new Make targets, deploy workflow behavior, wiki docs page, and ADR index.

## Tradeoffs and Risks
- Wiki remote may not exist until GitHub initializes it with a first wiki page; sync tool now reports this explicitly.
- Pages no longer publishes MkDocs output; docs are expected on wiki.
- Added script and policy surface area increases maintenance if repo URL strategy changes.

## How This Was Tested
- `uv run pytest -o addopts= tests/test_project_contracts.py`
- `uv run pre-commit run --files .github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml Makefile README.md docs/adr/README.md docs/adr/0018-wiki-docs-and-product-first-pages.md docs/deployment.md docs/github_collaboration.md docs/index.md docs/studio.md docs/wiki_docs.md mkdocs.yml tests/test_project_contracts.py tools/sync_wiki.py`
- Manual tool run: `uv run python tools/sync_wiki.py --wiki-dir .cache/story_generator.wiki`
- Manual repo setting update: enabled `has_wiki=true` via GitHub API.

## Follow-ups / Future Work
- Initialize first wiki page in GitHub UI if wiki git remote is still unavailable, then run `make wiki-sync-push` to publish mirrored docs.

### Motivation
- Provide an automated pipeline to capture daily MoonBit module statistics snapshots and generate diffs so history and changes are tracked in the repository.
- Enable daily automated execution at Beijing 10:00 (UTC 02:00) via GitHub Actions to keep `data/` and `diff/` up to date without manual intervention.

### Description
- Add `fetch.py` which downloads `https://mooncakes.io/api/v0/modules/statistics?raw=true` and saves the result to `data/YYYY-MM-DD.csv` using `requests`.
- Implement `diff.js` CLI that includes `parseCSV`, `compareCSV`, and `arrayToCSV`, compares rows by `name`, emits the requested columns (`name`, `status`, `line_count_diff`, `package_count_diff`, `csv1_line_count`, `csv1_package_count`, `csv2_line_count`, `csv2_package_count`) and writes output with a UTF-8 BOM.
- Add `run_daily.sh` to run the fetch and, if yesterday exists, run `node diff.js` to write `diff/YYYY-MM-DD.diff.csv` and mark the script executable.
- Add `.github/workflows/statistics.yml` to schedule the job at `cron: "0 2 * * *"`, set up Python 3.11 and Node 20, install `requests`, run `bash run_daily.sh`, and commit any changes to `data/` and `diff/`; also add `data/.gitkeep` and `diff/.gitkeep`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change; the GitHub Actions workflow is included and will run on schedule or via `workflow_dispatch` to exercise the pipeline automatically.

## Problem

The separate `docs-only-required-checks.yml` workflow caused job name mismatches with actual workflows, leaving required checks in perpetual "waiting for status" state. Maintaining duplicate job definitions across two files created unnecessary sync burden.

## Solution

Implemented inline path filtering using `dorny/paths-filter@v3` via a reusable workflow. Each workflow now:
- Calls a centralized reusable workflow for docs-only detection
- Runs minimal skip step when only docs changed (reports success)
- Runs full workflow when code/config changed
- Always reports a status check (no more "waiting")

### Pattern Applied

Created a reusable workflow to eliminate code duplication:

```yaml
# check-docs-only-changes.yml (reusable workflow)
on:
  workflow_call:
    outputs:
      docs_only:
        value: ${{ jobs.check-changes.outputs.docs_only }}

jobs:
  check-changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      docs_only: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.docs_only }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
        id: filter
        with:
          filters: |
            docs_only:
              - 'README.md'
              - 'CHANGELOG.md'
              - 'docs/**'
              - 'scripts/README.md'
```

Each workflow calls this reusable workflow:

```yaml
jobs:
  check-changes:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/check-docs-only-changes.yml

  actual-job:
    needs: check-changes
    steps:
      - name: Skip for docs-only changes
        if: needs.check-changes.outputs.docs_only == 'true'
        run: echo "Skipping - only documentation files changed"
      
      - name: Actual work
        if: needs.check-changes.outputs.docs_only != 'true'
        run: ...
```

Job names unchanged—branch protection rules remain valid. Existing triggers (push, workflow_dispatch, schedule) preserved.

Reusable workflow approach eliminates 84 lines of code duplication across workflow files, passing SonarCloud quality gates while improving maintainability with a single source of truth for docs-only detection logic.

xterm.js doesn't automatically maintain scroll position when large amounts of output are written via `term.write()`. This affected:
- Initial buffer replay when page loads
- Buffer replay when second client attaches to shared session
- Large output writes in general

## Solution

Added explicit scroll position preservation in three places:

1. **Initial setup** (line 947): Force scroll to bottom after fonts load and terminal fits
2. **WebSocket output** (line 1147): Check if at bottom before write, scroll back after if needed  
3. **P2P DataChannel output** (line 1088): Same preservation logic for P2P path

The preservation logic is smart:
- Only scrolls back to bottom if user was already there
- Allows users to scroll up to view history without interruption
- Uses `requestAnimationFrame` to ensure layout settles before scrolling

## Testing

- [x] Verified initial page load always starts at bottom
- [x] Verified connecting second client doesn't affect first client's scroll
- [x] All 401 tests pass

## Impact

Users can now:
- Reliably use shared sessions on desktop + mobile without scroll jumping
- Trust that the terminal will stay at the bottom when typing commands
- Scroll up to view history without being interrupted by new output

## Summary

close #1854

This PR adds explicit **no-wait** behavior for commit-wait TSO checks.

When `SetCommitWaitUntilTSO(...)` is enabled, users can now set
`SetCommitWaitUntilTSOTimeout(0)` to fail immediately if PD TSO is behind the expected commit-wait timestamp, instead of waiting.

## Motivation

In active-active replication scenarios, some callers prefer a fast-fail path rather than waiting for TSO catch-up. A zero timeout should represent this intent clearly.

## Behavior Change

- `commitWaitUntilTSOTimeout > 0`: keep existing bounded-wait behavior.
- `commitWaitUntilTSOTimeout == 0`: return `ErrCommitTSLag` immediately on the first lag check.
- Default behavior is unchanged because the transaction default timeout remains `1s`.

## Tests

Added integration coverage in `TestSetCommitWaitUntilTSO` for a new `"no wait"` case:

- enable commit-wait TSO;
- set timeout to `0`;
- mock lagging TSO;
- verify the commit path returns error immediately.

5. **Menú Contextual**: Ahora puedes convertir cualquier objeto de la escena en un prefab haciendo clic derecho y seleccionando "Guardar como Prefab".

### Motivation
- Some sources (Minfin, RG) returned 401/404/502/5xx or anti-bot pages and the harvester kept skipping them instead of recovering via warmup or Selenium fallback. 
- The HTTP client didn't recognise Qrator-style cookies as anti-bot protections and therefore missed cases where a warmup response set protection cookies.

### Description
- Added `"qrator"` to `_DDOS_GUARD_COOKIE_PREFIXES` and extended retry handling so `401`, `403`, and `404` statuses can trigger the Selenium warmup in `scripts/http_client.py`.
- Added per-source `request_strategy` entries for `Минфин России` and `Российская газета: Экономика` in `sources.json` to enable warmup requests, retries, custom headers, and Selenium fallback for those hosts.
- Added unit tests in `tests/test_http_client.py` to cover recognition of Qrator cookies during warmup and that `401` retry status triggers Selenium warmup.

### Testing
- Ran `pytest tests/test_http_client.py` which executed the HTTP client unit tests and all tests passed (`10 passed`).
- Ran `pytest tests/test_url_filters.py` which failed during collection with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scripts'` (test collection error unrelated to the changes in `http_client.py`).
- I exercised live requests to `https://minfin.gov.ru/` and `https://rg.ru/tema/ekonomika` to reproduce the observed 4xx/5xx and anti-bot behavior while designing warmup/retry settings.
